clue.text: Stonewall against the Australian blast in epic performance

parts.note: to stonewall is to obstruct or block
a southerly buster is a sudden cold wind in south-east Australia, so a buster is an Australian blast

explanation.surface: A defensive cricketer holds out against Australian hostility in a heroic innings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' simply sets the two pieces side by side. A southerly buster is a violent cold wind on Australia's south-east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A blockbuster is a lavish hit film or show, the sort of epic production audiences flock to.

clue.text: How one gets set when making an announcement

parts.note: these two words are what you get by shattering the phrase the news, with breaking as the anagram signal in the reading

explanation.surface: Someone asks how a person gets settled before delivering news.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange THE NEWS and you get SET WHEN, the clue's own words, with BREAKING as the anagram signal; the whole also means announcing something.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking the news is the idiom for telling someone important, often unwelcome, information.

clue.text: Twist a bit off the tree

indicators.note: a small piece is removed, so the final letter of the hero's first name is dropped

parts.note: Oliver Twist is Dickens's orphan hero, so Twist suggests his first name Oliver

explanation.surface: An instruction to snap a twig from a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit off' removes the final R from the name of Dickens's orphan.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive is a Mediterranean tree grown for its fruit and oil.

clue.text: Part of the lock at wharf, we hear's a dump

indicators.note: signals that the word for wharf is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a quay is a wharf for loading ships
a hole is a squalid, unpleasant place, a dump

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a dockside lock area is a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: QUAY is pronounced like KEY. 'at' and 's' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyhole is the opening in a lock into which the key goes.

clue.text: It's no good to economise

definitions.meaning: read as two words, it means consume a smaller amount, the way someone saving resources would

explanation.surface: Someone says there is no point trying to save money.
explanation.definitionFit: Useless means having no value or effect; split as use less it means to cut consumption.

clue.text: One with the will to try a rocky height

parts.note: to try something is to test it
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A determined climber sets out to tackle a rocky peak.
explanation.walkthrough: A TOR is a rocky hilltop, a word common in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is a person who has made a will, punning on having the will power.

clue.text: Produced by cricketing father and son, naturally?

definitions.text: Produced by cricketing father and son, naturally?

parts.words: Produced by cricketing father and son, naturally?
parts.note: cricket scores are made of runs, so a batting father and son both scoring them literally produce scores within one household, while the phrase also means an inherited trait

explanation.surface: A father and son both make cricket scores, as if by nature.
explanation.walkthrough: Runs are what batsmen score in cricket; the phrase also means a trait passed down in families.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that runs in the family is inherited, appearing naturally generation after generation.

clue.text: Birds with bird sounds to a degree

indicators.note: the bird sounds are added on after the degree

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree
caws are the harsh calls of crows and rooks

explanation.surface: Some birds are described as cawing up to a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to a degree' looks like 'somewhat', but it splits: the degree is a Master of Arts, and 'to' adds the crows' calls after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaws are large, brightly coloured parrots from Central and South America.

clue.text: The space traveller's remote after being set off

indicators.note: something set off is set going or disturbed, so the letters of remote are scrambled

explanation.surface: A spacecraft is said to be distant once launched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set off' reads like a launch, but it scrambles REMOTE; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteor is a piece of rock from space that streaks through the atmosphere.

clue.text: Pleasantness shown in matey arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement puts the letters of in matey into a new order

explanation.surface: Friendly behaviour is evident in a chummy setup.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenity can mean agreeableness or pleasantness of manner or place.

clue.text: City church's inner nature

parts.note: Essen is a city in Germany's Ruhr
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The spiritual heart of a city's church.
explanation.definitionFit: The essence of something is its intrinsic, fundamental character.

clue.text: Part of the joint where the spat took place?

definitions.text: Part of the joint where the spat took place?

parts.words: Part of the joint where the spat took place?
parts.note: a spat is a short gaiter worn over the shoe and lower leg, so it sits at a bone of that joint, while spat and joint suggest a quarrel in a pub

explanation.surface: A row broke out in a bar, and we ask exactly where.
explanation.walkthrough: Spats are old-fashioned cloth coverings for the instep and lower leg, not only quarrels; 'joint' is not a pub but a body joint.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle bone, the talus, forms part of the ankle joint, where a spat would be worn.

clue.text: A farmer's endlessly active

indicators.note: with no end, so the final letter of the farmer's name is dropped

parts.note: Farmer Giles is the stock name for a rustic farmer

explanation.surface: A farmer is described as tirelessly energetic.
explanation.walkthrough: Farmer Giles is a traditional British name for a typical farmer; 'endlessly' removes the S of GILES. The 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Agile means nimble and quick moving, so lively or active.

clue.text: Serving of venison sent back in the function

indicators.note: returning the portion means reading it from right to left
a portion is taken from within the word venison

explanation.surface: Venison is returned at a formal dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serving of' takes ENIS from inside venison and 'sent back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sine is a trigonometric function, the ratio of opposite side to hypotenuse.

clue.text: Tube to get the pulse going?

definitions.text: Tube to get the pulse going?

parts.words: Tube to get the pulse going?
parts.note: pulses are edible seeds such as dried peas, and a toy tube blows these out, rather than stirring a heartbeat

explanation.surface: Some medical device to restart a heartbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' suggests the heart, but pulses are also seeds like peas and lentils.
explanation.definitionFit: A peashooter is a small tube for blowing dried peas at a target.

clue.text: Safeguard the wildlife enclosure

definitions.meaning: to keep safe from harm or decay
a reserve where game or wild animals are protected

explanation.surface: A call to protect a nature reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve is to protect, and a preserve is an area kept for game or wildlife.

clue.text: Potentially hot stuff to teach in art school

indicators.note: to school is to train or drill, so the letters of teach in art are put into shape anew

explanation.surface: A sensational topic to cover at an art college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' reads as a noun but is the anagram signal; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthracite is hard coal, which burns hot once lit, so it is potentially hot.

clue.text: Snatch from sailor with a pipe

parts.note: AB is an able seaman
a duct is a pipe or channel carrying fluid or air

explanation.surface: Someone grabs something from a pipe-smoking seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: To abduct is to seize and carry someone off, to kidnap.

clue.text: How to keep a wild echidna?

definitions.text: How to keep a wild echidna?

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of echidna running out of control into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice on how to restrain an untamed spiny anteater.
explanation.walkthrough: An echidna is an Australian spiny anteater; mix up its letters and you have the way to restrain one.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping a wild animal fastened up with links of metal stops it escaping.

clue.text: Stuff with metal core at bottom of river

indicators.note: in a down entry, the core letters go beneath the river

parts.note: the Taff is a river in Wales running through Cardiff

indicators.note: the inner letters of metal, without its first and last

explanation.surface: Something packed with metal is dumped at a riverbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'core' takes ETA from metal, placed under TAFF, the Welsh river through Cardiff.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff is an old word for cloth, and taffeta is a crisp silk fabric.

clue.text: Look at drill going to-and-fro

parts.note: PE is physical education, the drill of school exercise

indicators.note: the piece goes one way and then back the other way

parts.note: the same physical education abbreviation again

explanation.surface: Inspect an exercise routine of back-and-forth movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to-and-fro' sets PE forwards then backwards; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To peep is to take a quick, furtive look.

clue.text: Place on the border needing a sign of security

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place in addresses
an edge is a border

explanation.surface: A spot on the frontier needs a security marker.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledge is something given as a guarantee or security for a promise.

clue.text: Riffraff finally ignored the rules

indicators.note: the last letter of the word ignored is picked out

parts.note: regs is short for regulations

explanation.surface: Lowlifes ended up disregarding the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Dregs are the lowest, most worthless part of a group, like riffraff.

clue.text: In trouble if I left AA as associate

indicators.note: troubled letters are disturbed, so if I left AA is rearranged

explanation.surface: A motorist who quit the breakdown service joins another one.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's Automobile Association breakdown service; here its letters are just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To affiliate is to associate or connect oneself with an organisation.

clue.text: Officer goes round most of cricket ground in a shade of green

indicators.note: the officer's letters surround the other piece

parts.note: LT is a lieutenant

indicators.note: most of something is nearly all of it, so the cricket ground's name loses its last letter

parts.note: the Oval is a London Test cricket ground

explanation.surface: An officer jogs around a cricket pitch dressed in green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims OVAL to OVA; THE OVAL is a London cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovat is a muted green colour, used chiefly in tweeds.

clue.text: Put on uniform as a sign of rank

definitions.text: Put on uniform as a sign of rank

parts.words: Put on uniform as a sign of rank
parts.note: describes a V-shaped stripe sewn to a sleeve to show grade, while reading like instructions to get dressed

explanation.surface: Someone dons uniform to show status.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevron is a V-shaped stripe on a military sleeve showing rank.

clue.text: Wishing to have leaderless soldiers competing

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for soldiers is removed

parts.note: men are ordinary soldiers
vying means competing

explanation.surface: Troops without a commander are fighting among themselves for what they want.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaderless' removes the M of MEN, leaving EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Envying means coveting or wanting what someone else possesses.

clue.text: Firm demolished flats internally with determination

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the word for firm

parts.note: steady means firm

indicators.note: a demolished block is knocked down, so the letters of flats are scrambled

explanation.surface: A company knocked down a block of flats resolutely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company in the surface, but it is the adjective meaning steady, which holds the knocked-down flats.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadfastly means resolutely and unwaveringly.
